tasks.short: Prepare or check food trays against prescribed diets

steps.what: Check prescribed diet and patient identity before preparing or inspecting the tray
Prepare or examine food trays for conformance to the prescribed diet

tasks.design: Retain checking the actual tray against current diet instructions from the {OTHER} clinical record. A diet label supports the nurse but does not establish that the food on the tray conforms.
tasks.previous_blocker: Correct labels and the actual prepared food may differ.
tasks.enabler_now: Record access can show current instructions without inspecting the tray.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising substitutions, unidentified ingredients or changed restrictions.
tasks.human_edge: Stop and clarify an uncertain tray rather than infer that it is safe.
tasks.altitude: No change to diet authority or tray checking time.

reach.learn: Diet codes, ingredient information and escalation limits

evidence.claim: Diet compliance requires matching the real food tray to current instructions; a recorded diet code alone does not inspect food.

assumptions: Boundary covers this nurse's preparation or examination, not diet prescription or kitchen production. Kitchen work is outside and unchanged when the nurse examines a prepared tray.

The responsible clinician or dietitian produces patient identifier, diet instruction, restrictions and effective time through existing care work outside this boundary. The nurse reconciles these in s1 and inspects food in s2; all capture and checks remain counted.
Missing instructions, unknown food identity or unclear restrictions trigger direct clarification or tray replacement through the existing route, not inferred compliance.
Test native current-diet display first; no new inspection system or automated meal decision is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because the process remains unchanged.
unknowns: Division of tray preparation work and current diet-change communication
research_questions: Where do discrepancies arise between the latest diet instruction and the actual tray?

already_counted.description: Instruction checks and physical tray work remain.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, net=0. Standard trays and uncertain ingredients both retain current-instruction and physical conformance checks.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain procedures and prepare patients for examinations, tests or treatment

steps.what: Explain the procedure and clarify patient questions and readiness concerns
Prepare patients physically for examinations, tests or treatments and escalate concerns

tasks.design: Retain explanation and physical preparation by the nurse, with current instructions available through the {OTHER} clinical record. A digital checklist may support the existing process but does not replace readiness assessment or hands-on work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Patients need individual explanation and practical help, with changing clinical concerns.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing instructions can be accessible without removing care time.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising when preparation instructions conflict with the patient's current condition.
tasks.human_edge: Notice anxiety or an unresolved concern and involve the responsible clinician.
tasks.altitude: No change in preparation responsibility or procedural authority.

reach.learn: Readiness checks and escalation within local scope

evidence.claim: Patient explanation and physical procedure preparation remain direct care activities.

assumptions: Boundary covers nurse explanation and preparation, not procedure selection, consent authorisation or the test itself.

The procedure team supplies procedure identifier, patient, timing and preparation instructions through existing work outside this boundary, unchanged. The nurse checks understanding and readiness in s1 and s2, retaining all assessment and capture effort.
No ready-to-proceed flag is assumed. Missing or conflicting instructions use direct clarification before proceeding.
Test native instruction access before any custom checklist; none is introduced.
Zero incremental upkeep because care and tools remain unchanged. Professional scope is verified locally.
unknowns: Procedure mix, local scope and available communication support
research_questions: Which preparation failures arise from instruction access rather than necessary patient contact?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, net=0. Routine preparation and patients requiring extra clarification retain all contact and physical work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Provide nursing and personal care at home and teach simple care tasks

steps.what: Provide home medical treatment, personal care, comfort and household support within scope
Instruct family members in simple nursing tasks and check understanding

tasks.design: Retain home care and family instruction with the nurse, supported by the existing {OTHER} home-care record. No record tool performs cooking, physical care, reassurance or practical family demonstration.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work depends on a changing home environment and direct personal help.
tasks.enabler_now: Mobile care records can support continuity without replacing this service.
tasks.still_hard: Adapting care to the home and recognising when family members need additional support.
tasks.human_edge: Notice discomfort, preserve dignity and teach a task at a pace the caregiver can manage.
tasks.altitude: Home care responsibility and time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Hands-on home care and caregiver instruction require direct physical and relational work.

assumptions: Boundary is the nurse's home visit care and instruction, not travel, scheduling or a separate visit note. Treatment remains within local professional scope and instructions.

Responsible care professionals produce the existing home plan outside this boundary, unchanged. The nurse checks present needs during s1 and family understanding during s2; no structured comfort or caregiver-competence feed is assumed.
Unclear instructions or insufficient caregiver capacity require clarification or escalation within retained care time.
Native mobile care-plan access is considered first; no new tool or capture process is introduced.
Zero incremental upkeep because there is no changed process. Broad home-care work overlapping narrower care tasks is allocated once.
unknowns: Visit mix, scope and available family support
research_questions: Are any clerical visit tasks separately measurable without reducing direct care?

already_counted.description: Home care and family instruction remain.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, net=0. Routine visits and homes requiring more support retain direct care and instruction time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Make appointments and maintain clinic records

steps.what: Clarify appointment or clerical request and verify patient and administrative details
Make appointments and confirm the selected slot with the patient
Keep clinic records current and file verified clerical documents

tasks.design: Configure native appointment and administrative record functions in the {OTHER} clinic system, with {CALENDAR} slot views where already supported. The nurse captures the request, confirms the exact booking and checks filing; direct entry avoids separate paper lists and repeated copying where they exist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper requests and separate appointment or filing lists can require duplicate entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native scheduling and records functions can reuse verified administrative details.
tasks.still_hard: Clarifying ambiguous requests and identifying instructions that require clinical review.
tasks.human_edge: Know when an administrative request cannot be processed without clinician clarification.
tasks.altitude: Less appointment navigation and duplicate filing; no new triage or treatment authority.

reach.task: Help a patient resolve an appointment access problem
reach.learn: Booking rules, accessibility needs and escalation routes

evidence.claim: Native appointment and administrative records functions can avoid duplicate entry while retaining patient verification and exception handling.

assumptions: Boundary covers mixed clinic clerical work, not clinical assessment, transcription or urgency decisions. The split and paper duplication are E1 scenarios, not measured facts.

The nurse captures patient identifier, verified contact, request type, requested service, clinician-specified appointment duration and any accessibility need in s1. Clinical service, urgency and duration come from the responsible clinician's existing instructions outside this boundary, unchanged; missing instructions trigger manual clarification.

The scheduling owner produces provider, location, slot time, duration and booking rules through existing schedule maintenance, unchanged. The nurse checks availability and patient agreement in retained s2 time; conflicts use manual coordination, never automatic triage.

Record identifier, document type, date and source are checked and captured by the nurse in retained s3 time; no free structured filing index is assumed. Unreadable documents remain in a manual clarification queue.
Test native scheduling, direct filing and duplicate checks first. Existing automated bookings earn no new labour saving.
unknowns: Native functions, existing duplication and actual clerical mix
research_questions: Do direct booking and filing reduce nurse time after counting all request capture, confirmation and uncertain documents?

already_counted.description: Request clarification and identity checks remain.
Booking checks and patient confirmation remain.
Record-field capture, filing checks and exceptions remain.

incremental.description: Nurse checks duplicate records and recurring booking or filing exceptions.
Clinic system owner maintains booking rules and filing permissions.

approvals.approved_version: Exact patient, service, provider, location, time, duration and contact confirmation reviewed at booking; changes require renewed confirmation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=65, gross=35 less three focal upkeep hours gives net=32. High assumes booking and filing effort halve where duplicate paper work exists; low assumes current native functions already remove most duplication, leaving only upkeep-equivalent gains. Clarification remains unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Tray checks, procedure preparation and home care retain full direct-care time. Native clinic clerical functions can reduce verified duplicate booking and filing work.
reach: Improve preparation and home-care handovers with registered nurses
Resolve administrative access issues with patient representatives
role.ambitious_version: A nurse who spends less time copying clinic information while keeping direct care, clinical judgement and patient communication within verified scope.
